tagline: A freeway over the pass, through a city's wild park.
intro: East of Santo Road the SR 52 freeway leaves Tierrasanta and crosses Mission Trails Regional Park, a preserve of rugged canyons and hills, for about three and a half miles. It climbs to Mission Trails Pass north of Fortuna Mountain and comes down toward Mast Boulevard and the San Diego River, with a two-way bicycle path along its north side the whole way.

The road cuts show the age of the ground, Eocene rock about 50 million years old with marine fossils, and on the east side of the mountain granitic rock of about 150 million. The freeway took more than fifty years to finish, held up along the way by a songbird, the least Bell's vireo.

moments.title: Fortuna Mountain
moments.text: The northernmost of the five peaks in the middle of the park stands up plainly over the lower mesas as the freeway crosses the summit between San Diego and Santee.

moments.title: Old Mission Dam
moments.text: Probably prompted by the drought of 1800 to 1802, the mission dammed the San Diego River here in 1803 to water the fields of Mission San Diego de Alcalá, five miles off.

moments.title: Kumeyaay Lake
moments.text: A gravel pit that turned into a small lake among riparian and chaparral plants, with a campground of 46 sites on its bank.
